method: Single elimination in a power-of-two bracket. The bracket is rounded up to the next power of two, so a 12-team field is drawn as a 16-place bracket and the four spare places become byes; a bracket with n teams always plays n-1 matches over log2(size) rounds. Standard seeding builds the slot order recursively: the order starts as 1, 2, and each doubling appends 2m+1 minus each existing seed, which gives 1 v 8, 4 v 5, 2 v 7, 3 v 6 for eight places, so every first-round pair sums to one more than the bracket size and seeds 1 and 2 land in opposite halves and can meet only in the final. Seeds above the team count become byes, so byes go to the best seeds; those matches advance their single entrant automatically and never count as played matches. Entry order instead fills the draw top to bottom in the order the teams are listed and gives the byes to the last first-round matches, one per match, so no first-round match is empty. Clicking a team records the winner of that match and fills the next round from it; clicking the recorded winner again clears the pick, and a later pick that no longer has both of its teams present is dropped rather than carried forward. Inputs are limited to 2 to 32 whole teams, names of 40 characters or fewer that must be unique ignoring case, and the two draw orders; text, fractional, negative, zero, one and out-of-range team counts, an unsupported draw order and a name count that disagrees with the team count are refused with the field named. The page stores nothing, sends nothing and makes no network requests.

sources.title: Tournament practice: a single-elimination bracket is drawn to the next power of two, with byes filling the spare places so the whole field fits.
Standard bracket seeding: each first-round pairing sums to one more than the bracket size, which keeps the top two seeds in opposite halves.
Unseeded draws are filled in entry order and byes are spread across the trailing first-round matches, so no match has two empty places.
